RAM, CPUs, lifetime and keep-alive are configurable. Disk management supports offline expansion/shrink, compaction and a retained recovery disk. Stock networking uses a proxy and explicit UDP/ping; the custom kernel optionally adds ordinary TCP/UDP/DNS. Direct USB, GPU Vulkan and hardware video remain unavailable.

Android’s kernel, boot partitions and SELinux stay unchanged; no Android reboot. Choose stock Microdroid or a verified guest image in private app storage. Root and Gunyah are required. This route has no pvmfw verified boot or equivalent AVF guarantee.

1. Open Prepare Debian, stop the launcher, then download or import the image.\n2. Enable the VM connection and open Debian terminal. GUI setup can be run there with plb-install-gui.\n3. Vector is only needed for optional stock Terminal integration; select Terminal as its only scope.
Terminal and its installer are enabled.
Could not enable Terminal. Check root permission and whether this OS includes the stock Terminal.
This OS or Terminal version is untested. The bridge is disabled for compatibility.

Network egress uses the selected Android app UID and its INTERNET permission, VPN and power policy. Terminal is the default; the experimental profile can explicitly choose Bridge for its fullscreen GUI. Background/Doze restrictions can block either app. No host routes, DNS, firewall or power restrictions are changed.

Run plb-install-gpu inside Linux, then save graphics settings here and recreate only the VM. Android restart is unnecessary. virgl (Adreno) in plb-gpu-info indicates host GPU OpenGL. Weston composition and direct Android GPU viewing have separate switches. Capture and copying still use CPU. Zero-copy and GPU Vulkan are not supported.

ping -c 4 1.1.1.1 sends real IPv4 echo requests without raw sockets. plb-udp-forward 5353 1.1.1.1 53 forwards guest localhost:5353 to the specified UDP destination until interrupted. Configure your tool to use that local port. This is explicit forwarding, not transparent networking. Host-local, link-local and multicast destinations are blocked.

Resolution, frame-rate cap and Linux graphics apply at the next VM start. Reopen the viewer to change display transport. First run plb-install-gpu inside Linux. Saved Bridge settings override guest mode commands at VM startup. The fps selection is an upper limit; actual speed depends on the display, VM and application.
This closes all Linux sessions. Save your Linux work first. Android will not restart.

Linux root and sudo apply inside the VM. Android files are not shared. The GPU decoder is unprivileged, but the host VMM currently runs as root without its normal process sandbox. This is not a fully hardened environment for untrusted code; host/hypervisor/GPU bugs may affect Android.
Keep the VM after closing all views

Resource changes apply next VM start. This capacity menu only expands; use VMs → Disk management for offline shrinking, compaction and recovery disks. Memory and CPUs require host headroom. Background survival depends on Android and root.
Save and recreate only the VM
Closes all Linux sessions. Save your work first. Android is not restarted.

Run plb-install-integration in Linux once. Speaker works in the Bridge fullscreen GUI. Microphone is OFF by default. Choose GUI only or Background; background capture uses an Android microphone service with a Stop action. Android microphone permission is required. Clipboard sharing is text only, up to 64 KiB; start the Linux GUI first.
Could not start background microphone. Open Bridge and check microphone permission.

Select wired, USB or Bluetooth devices already connected to Android. OFF keeps Linux on built-in audio; ON routes Linux streams to the devices below. This forwards audio, not exclusive device ownership. Android apps keep their routing. Reopen the GUI after changes. Classic Bluetooth microphone availability depends on Android exposing an input route.
Use connected devices for Linux audio

The installed crosvm disables direct USB in protected VMs, even with guest USB drivers. USB/Bluetooth audio can instead use Android’s per-stream audio bridge above. No physical peripheral was available for testing.

Choose stock Microdroid or experimental Linux 6.18.57-plb1. Experimental use copies Debian into a separate disk, initially 512 MiB / 1 CPU / CPU graphics. Gunyah memory allocation can terminate the VM under heavier workloads. Android’s kernel and boot partitions stay unchanged; host-failure risk is not zero.

Save Linux work first. Only the current VM will stop. First experimental use copies and verifies the whole disk, requiring time and free device storage. The original disk is retained. Android will not reboot.
Selected: stock Microdroid / original Debian disk

Could not complete the switch. Check kernel installation, storage and root. Select stock Microdroid to reopen the original environment.

Stop this VM and use 512 MiB, 1 CPU, 960 × 540 at 30 fps, Openbox with GPU apps and the GPU viewer. Disk size and other resource settings are retained. This reduces memory pressure; it does not guarantee stability. Reopen the GUI afterwards.

TCP, UDP and DNS without per-app proxy settings, using a TUN interface inside the custom-kernel VM. Android routing and firewall stay unchanged. DNS uses 1.1.1.1 / 8.8.8.8; traffic follows the selected Android app’s network/VPN policy. Background restrictions on that app may block it; choose Bridge for its GUI. No incoming ports, broadcast or arbitrary IP protocols. Ping uses the existing plb-ping relay.
Stop this VM to apply. Open Terminal or GUI again to start it. No Android restart. The guest resolver change lasts only for this boot.
Requires the experimental Linux kernel profile. Stock mode keeps its existing proxy.

Save Linux work first. This stops only this VM. Resize and compaction create and verify offline copies. The previous disk is retained. Restoring swaps the two disks, retaining both. Android will not reboot.
Delete the previous recovery disk permanently? The current disk is retained. This cannot be undone.

Applies to the selected Debian profile. Thin qcow2 grows with use. Virtual capacity, Android allocation and Linux usage are different. Shrink requires enough room for data and filesystem metadata. Copies need additional temporary space. Free-space recovery zeroes unused blocks on a copy; the current disk is never truncated. A retained previous disk must be restored or explicitly deleted before another resize/compaction.
Linux usage is available while the VM is running.

Disk operation did not complete. The original is retained. Check private storage logs before retrying; an interrupted promotion is recovered at next start.

Run a separate Android 17 VM. The experimental 4096 MiB profile uses Adreno GLES; other profiles use software rendering. The 480 × 800 viewer supports taps and swipes, with slow image capture. Startup is not yet reliable. Prepared OS images are required. Each profile preserves its own data.

Requires the inspected SM-S948Q Android 17 ROM and Terminal 37.

1536 MiB and 1792 MiB refuse startup if host page-management failures are recorded. 1792 MiB is an unverified experiment, not a successful memory measurement. These modes temporarily use up to 6 GiB of RAM during preparation. Background apps may be reclaimed. Startup changes the host-wide 16/32/64 KiB shmem THP settings to advise for about 10 seconds, then restores them. An independent guardian attempts restoration at its 40-second deadline on failure.\n\nOn first use, each larger preset copies the original 512 MiB Android disks. Each preset stores later data independently. Debian is stopped and its disks are preserved. Closing this viewer stops only this VM. Maximum session: 30 minutes. These legacy presets do not support guest networking, audio, physical USB or GPU rendering. The separate 4096 MiB GPU profile has its own six-key confirmation.
Preparing Android guest memory… (maximum allocation budget: 6 GiB)
Could not prepare the selected RAM preset’s disk copy. Existing Android disks are retained. Check available storage and logs.

The larger RAM presets require the pinned SM-S948Q / S948QOPS1AZHL host environment. Select 512 MiB on this environment.

The host has recorded a page-management failure. This large-memory session was not started. Host settings and existing VM disks were left unchanged.
The pinned Android GPU runtime is missing from this APK. Use a GPU-enabled release build; the existing profiles remain available.

Gunyah could not map guest RAM. This startup failure can recur even with enough free RAM. This VM was stopped without retrying; choose an existing profile or try again manually later. Android was not restarted.

This separate Android 17 profile has reached the home screen and passed Adreno GLES readback, but startup is unreliable and may fail with Gunyah ENOMEM. Optional IPv4 networking relays TCP and UDP through the Bridge app. Vulkan, audio and USB remain unsupported. GPU texture display is selected by default and does not capture screenshots. Turning GPU display off explicitly selects the slower raw/PNG capture mode. Zero-copy and 60 presented fps are not established.

Each launch explicitly permits temporary host-wide shmem THP advice for exactly 16/32/64/128/256/512 KiB. The six original never settings are restored as soon as RAM is prepared, with an independent 40-second restoration guardian. Other applications requesting hugepages may be affected during that window. Preparation uses up to 6 GiB RAM; background applications may close. A kernel/hypervisor failure can still stop Android and lose temporary root. Recorded host page-management failures refuse startup.

Total guest RAM is 4096 MiB, including a 128 MiB shared DMA pool. The separate guest kernel/VMM and new persistent disks stay in app-private storage. Existing Debian and Android profiles remain intact. Closing the viewer stops this VM. Maximum session: 30 minutes. No automatic retry or host reboot.

Uses a separate copy of the prepared 4 GiB guest. Prepare the existing 4 GiB profile first. Uses a GPU texture instead of screenshot transfer; 60 fps and zero-copy are not established. Closing the viewer ends this VM. The existing display mode remains available.

Separate Android 17 guest with 4096 MiB RAM and Adreno GLES. GPU transfer uses a separate disk copy. Startup may fail with Gunyah ENOMEM; the next screen explains the temporary host-wide settings and RAM preparation before launch.

Allocated bytes are host filesystem blocks; file size is not QCOW2 virtual capacity or guest free space. Shared/hard-linked files can be counted more than once. Android 17 / S948QOPU1BZI9 only. Host identity and a small protected CPU VM with read-only Debian dpkg were verified. New setup, backup/restore, writable sessions and GPU viewing await device tests. Android guest launch remains disabled; existing disks are retained.

Backups are not encrypted. Guest disks may contain passwords, accounts and personal files. Choose a trusted storage location with enough space. A failed or cancelled export leaves an incomplete file; delete it before trying again.

Install the ARM64 Debian image from Google directly into Bridge. A download is about 580 MiB; allow at least 7 GiB free for the installed image and first private VM disk. No stock Terminal window or Vector is needed to use the in-app terminal and desktop. Root and the exact supported ROM are still required.

Choose an input port when more than one is exposed. Android may combine physical microphones into one processed mono stream; descriptor counts do not prove the number of physical microphones. Direction is a HAL preference, not independent capsule selection. These controls apply to Debian; Android guest microphone forwarding is not connected yet.
Experimental Android 17 · 1 GiB RAM · GLES direct display. Uses the separately prepared Android 17 disk profile. No session time limit. Optional Internet is configured inside the guest.

Start the 1 GiB Android 17 guest? The dedicated h17mfix disk must already be prepared; this APK contains no Android OS image. Six approved host-wide shmem THP settings are temporarily changed for RAM preparation and restored within 40 seconds by an independent guardian. Unhealthy or fragmented memory refuses startup without retry. There is no session duration limit: closing the viewer, guest shutdown, crashes or monitored host failures stop the owned VM. Internet uses a guest-only virtual interface and an unprivileged host relay; host VPN, routes and DNS are unchanged. Vulkan and physical camera/microphone forwarding remain disabled. Close other Bridge VMs first. Host crashes remain possible.
This APK does not contain the compatible Android 17 runtime. Install the signed experimental build with the pinned runtime.

Debian only: allow plb-torch status / off / on [level [seconds]] while the Bridge terminal or desktop is visible. Select an LED first. Default OFF; each ON lasts at most 30 seconds. Closing the view, disconnecting or revoking consent releases this session’s light. CameraManager does not provide exclusive ownership: other apps can still change the LED. Android guest flash HAL is not connected yet.
